column1: # Verdicts of real kmod for install directives (FREES-190). Each name was written as
# 'install <name> /bin/echo HIT' to /etc/modprobe.d/00.conf of the pinned Ubuntu 24.04 (kmod 31) and
# Rocky Linux 9 (kmod 28) images, with the host's module tree mounted read-only and no network.
# Columns: module, verdict of 'modprobe -n -v <module>' (MATCH: the install command runs, NOMATCH,
# REJECT: 'ignoring bad line'), the name as 'modprobe -c -d /dev -C <file>' printed it ('-' when it
# printed none), and the name as written. Both kmods gave the same verdict for every row. The table
# holds every MATCH row, every row on which the round-2 or the current filter differs from kmod and
# 800 other rows, out of 27931 names times 2 modules.
